title: AdaRank: Adaptive Rank Pruning for Enhanced Model Merging
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Dominant leading components of a task vector help their own task but hurt other tasks, so naive rank truncation is flawed.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, paired bar charts then line plot, shared x-axis
description: A wide, short figure with three plots that share the x-axis, the singular component index r. Panels (a) TA and (b) CART are bar charts. Each has a dashed zero line. Blue bars below zero show the change in single-task loss, and orange bars show the change in multi-task loss. The orange bars are tall and positive at the lowest indices, so the top components raise loss on other tasks, and they shrink and fluctuate at higher indices. A shared legend sits above the two bar charts. Panel (c) is a line plot of loss change for eight datasets (Cars, DTD, EuroSAT, GTSRB, MNIST, RESISC45, SUN397, SVHN). MNIST is a dashed purple line that dips deeply negative at small r, while other tasks rise positive. All curves converge to zero by about r=30. A vertical divider separates (c) from (a) and (b).
caption: (a), (b) Net change in single-task and multi-task losses for Task Arithmetic [ref] and CART [ref], respectively, when each singular component of a target task vector is individually added to a model merged with full-rank vectors from other tasks. (c) Loss changes of all tasks when adding singular components from the MNIST task vector, with MNIST shown as a dotted line. For clarity, only the top 10% of singular components are shown.
abstract: Model merging has emerged as a promising approach for unifying independently fine-tuned models into an integrated framework, significantly enhancing computational efficiency in multi-task learning. Recently, several SVD-based techniques have been introduced to exploit low-rank structures for enhanced merging, but their reliance on such manually designed rank selection often leads to cross-task interference and suboptimal performance. In this paper, we propose AdaRank, a novel model merging framework that adaptively selects the most beneficial singular directions of task vectors to merge multiple models. We empirically show that the dominant singular components of task vectors can cause critical interference with other tasks, and that naive truncation across tasks and layers degrades performance. In contrast, AdaRank dynamically prunes the singular components that cause interference and offers an optimal amount of information to each task vector by learning to prune ranks during test-time via entropy minimization. Our analysis demonstrates that such method mitigates detrimental overlaps among tasks, while empirical results show that AdaRank consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance with various backbones and number of tasks, reducing the performance gap between fine-tuned models to nearly 1%.
